summary.headline: Polycab Q1 FY27: consolidated revenue up 39% YoY, record PAT of INR 7,967 million (+33% YoY), EBITDA margin 13.8%.
summary.overview: Consolidated revenue grew 39% YoY with EBITDA up 32% and margin at 13.8%, about 70 bps sequentially higher. Record quarterly PAT of INR 7,967 million at a 9.7% margin. Wires & Cables grew 39% and FMEG grew 71%, while EPC revenue fell 11%. Volume growth in domestic cables and wires was low to mid-single digit against a high base of about 26% last year, and exports declined on the Middle East disruption. Management cut prices by 3-4% in early July and said channel destocking followed the sharp fall in copper and aluminium prices in June.

financial_highlights.change: improved significantly, aided by temporary rise in payable days from LC usage

segments.name: Wires & Cables
segments.commentary: Segment revenue grew 39% YoY; domestic W&C grew 43% YoY with domestic volume growth of low to mid-single digits. Segment EBIT margin was 13.3%, supported by wires mix, channel mix and operations; exports were a drag.

segments.name: FMEG
segments.commentary: Revenue grew 71% YoY, the tenth straight quarter of outperforming industry growth. EBIT margin was 8%; premium mix reached about 25% of the portfolio (fans about 33%, lighting about 38%). Solar more than doubled and is now the largest category, though still below 50% of FMEG.

segments.name: EPC
segments.commentary: Revenue was INR 3,077 million, down 11% YoY on project timing; profitability was INR 338 million at an 11% margin. Management attributed the dip to milestone-linked revenue recognition.

guidance_outlook: Wires & Cables medium- to long-term EBIT margin guidance maintained at 11% to 13% under Project Spring.
FMEG targets EBITDA margins of 8% to 10% by FY30 (full-year basis) and growth at 1.5x to 2x industry growth.
EPC: sustainable operating margins expected in the high single-digit range over the medium to long term.
Management reiterated 1.5x market growth on volume plus value; FY26 volume growth was 18%.
Working capital cycle expected to normalise to the 45 to 50 day range as LC-related payable effects unwind.
Exports guided to exceed 10% of consolidated top line by 2030. Management expects a sizable US export pickup in the coming quarters.
EPC: Bharat Net and RDSS together expected to contribute about INR 800-1,000 crores (Bharat Net) and about INR 800 crores (RDSS) this year; combined order book about INR 10,900 crores.
capex_capacity: Q1 FY27 capex was INR 3.2 billion.
Bharat Net order is about INR 8,000 crores, of which INR 4,500 crores is an execution piece over about 3 years; fibre for the execution period is already secured.
Data-centre opportunity estimated at 8-16/18 GW versus about 1.6 GW installed base; management cites INR 20,000-25,000 crores of cable market over 5-8 years.
T&D: about 2,000 circuit km added in April-May FY27; CEA estimate of about 17,000 ckm for FY27 versus about 20,000-21,000 ckm average for FY26-FY30.
demand_pricing: Domestic W&C volume growth was low to mid-single digit on a base of about 26% last year (cables above 25%, wires above 20%); wires grew high single digit and cables low to mid single digit.
Price revision of about 3-4% taken in the first fortnight of July 2026; pricing is cost-plus and passes through copper movements.
Channel stocking was below expectation in June as aluminium fell about 18-20% and copper fell from about INR 14,000 to INR 13,100-13,200; healthy channel stocking is about 20-25 days.
Exports declined YoY (about 13% per analyst); Middle East was about 20-24% of Q1 exports, North America 45-50% (US about 50%), Europe 18-20%. Order book is healthy in US, Europe and Latin America.
Channel contributes about 90% of W&C sales; Polycab estimates it gained 3-4% market share over the last 10-12 months (per last update).
FMEG: fans, pipes and conduits, lighting and switchgear all grew faster than their industry categories; FMEG ex-solar volume and price split not disclosed.

qa_highlights.question: What were the price hikes and volume growth YoY, and how will pricing look in Q2 given copper?
qa_highlights.answer: Domestic cable and wire volume grew low to mid-single digit on a high base; no Q2 copper guidance given, as pricing is cost-plus. A 3-4% price revision was taken in early July.

qa_highlights.question: Acceptances rose; how much are LC/acceptances and is their interest booked in finance costs?
qa_highlights.answer: Inventory is about 100-110 days, LC-based payables about 80-90 days, and receivables 20-30 days, producing a 15-day cycle this quarter. The accounting treatment was deferred to an offline discussion.

qa_highlights.question: Data-centre and optical fibre opportunity, and export trends?
qa_highlights.answer: Data centres could add about INR 3.5 crores of cable per MW, an INR 20,000-25,000 crore market over 6-8 years, and Polycab already supplies conventional cables to some existing sites. Exports are recovering with a healthy order book; Middle East was 20-24% of Q1 exports.

qa_highlights.question: Bharat Net fibre price risk and why EPC revenue fell?
qa_highlights.answer: Fibre for the execution period is already secured, so Bharat Net is not exposed to higher fibre prices. EPC revenue timing is milestone-linked and may shift between quarters, with no material full-year dip expected.

qa_highlights.question: Full-year volume growth outlook and market share?
qa_highlights.answer: Management pointed to 10-12 month trends rather than quarters; FY26 volume growth was 18% and 1.5x market growth is reiterated. Share gains of 3-4% were reported in the last update, with the next analysis expected after peers report.

qa_highlights.question: Are there signs of channel stocking benefiting Q1, and is the margin improvement limited?
qa_highlights.answer: Stocking was below expectation as raw-material prices fell in June. Margins were supported by wires mix and channel mix, offset by weaker exports and operating leverage; the company targets the 11-13% range.

qa_highlights.question: What is the FMEG margin trajectory, and is 8% EBIT sustainable?
qa_highlights.answer: Drivers were operating leverage on a low base, a premium mix of about 25% overall, and regional product strategies. Management expects seasonality and targets 8-10% EBITDA margin for FMEG for full year.

qa_highlights.question: Is the data-centre and T&D demand strong enough to move industry growth, given the TAM?
qa_highlights.answer: Management agreed that 1 GW of data-centre additions alone would be limited, but said T&D demand is accelerating, with about 15% cable content in T&D spend and transformer makers' order books at about 2.5x revenue.

risks_watch: Copper and aluminium volatility: June price falls led to destocking, and a 3-4% price cut was taken in early July.
Export recovery depends on Middle East and US trade conditions; exports declined YoY in Q1 with the Middle East impacted from March.
Working capital cycle of 15 days is flattered by LC-based payables and is expected to revert to 45-50 days.
Volume growth was low to mid-single digit against a high base; management points to a 10-12 month trend rather than quarters.
Data-centre and T&D demand timing is uncertain; CEA's 17,000 ckm FY27 target versus a 14,000-15,000 ckm five-year average was questioned by an analyst.
EPC revenue is lumpy and milestone-linked; Bharat Net and RDSS execution depends on milestones.
Geopolitical and energy-price volatility, including Strait of Hormuz disruptions and a renewed Iran-US flare-up.
summary.management_tone: Confident on demand and long-term growth, but cautious on near-term volume and exports. Management was evasive on Q2 pricing, the acceptance-interest accounting and the FMEG product split, and deferred several questions offline.
key_quotes: We remain confident in the medium-term outlook for the Indian economy and the robust demand environment it continues to create for our business.
It's like you are aware, it's a cost-plus model. So whatever is the cost, we'll pass it on, and we'll continue to focus on the business.
So I think over a period of 10 to 12 months is a good time to look at a trend.
